issues.title: Radial moment estimate lacks p-power factors
issues.failure_explanation: For Λ=ℤ, h=1, p=2, V_1=[1/2,3/2), and μ=δ_{0.51}, the claimed left side is 1, whereas h^2 rad(V_0)^2+M_2(μ)=0.25+0.2601<1. The proof incorrectly infers |x|^p≥||hλ|^p-rad(V_{hλ})^p|. The valid implication is |hλ|≤|x|+h rad(V_0), which introduces factors 2^{p-1}.
issues.overall_effect: Item (i) of the lemma is quantitatively false. Its later uses only need finiteness of the corresponding moments, which the corrected constant-factor estimate supplies, so the stated Wasserstein approximation rates need not change.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace item (i) of LEM:RadialEstimates by ∑λ |hλ|^p μ(V_{hλ}) ≤ 2^(p-1)[M_p(μ)+h^p rad(V_0)^p]. Prove it from |hλ| ≤ |x|+h rad(V_0) for x in V_{hλ}, and propagate only the resulting constant changes through the finite-moment checks.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes an invalid inference after taking p-th powers, so this is not transcriptional. The triangle inequality and the standard power bound give a short, routine local repair; only inessential constants change, while finiteness, the construction, and all Wasserstein rates remain unchanged.

issues.title: Fixed-lattice N-term cell count

failure_location.quote:
Note that for any $h\in(0,1]$, $\mu_h$ has at most \[\mc{N}(B_R,hV_{0}) \leq 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}(B_R,V_0) = 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}\]
terms

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given two convex bodies $K$ and $T$, let $\mc{N}(K,T)$ be the minimal number of translates of $T$ it takes to cover $K$

issues.failure_explanation: The covering number counts the smallest number of arbitrary translates of hV_0 covering B_R; it is not the number of cells from the fixed hΛ tiling that meet the support. Moreover, h=3(𝒩/N)^{1/d} need not be at most 1. For example, in d=2 take a rectangular lattice with V_0=[-1/M,1/M]×[-b/2,b/2], b>2R and R=1, so 𝒩(B_R,V_0)=M. For N=1 the prescribed h=3√M, while the scaled cell width is 6/√M; for large M several fixed cells meet the interior of B_R. A measure assigning positive mass in two such cells makes μ_h have more than one term.
issues.overall_effect: The all-N term-count assertion in THM:NTermDirac is false, and the piecewise-constant N-term corollary mimics the same counting step. The asymptotic Wasserstein estimate can still be recovered for sufficiently large N with a genuine fixed-cell count.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate THM:NTermDirac and its piecewise-constant dependent result for N ≥ 3^d 𝒩(B_R,V_0), retaining h=3(𝒩/N)^(1/d). Replace the arbitrary-cover count by a fixed-cell volume argument: if k cells of hΛ meet B_R, their union lies in B_R+2hV_0, so k h^d|V_0| ≤ 𝒩(B_R,V_0)(1+2h)^d|V_0| and hence k ≤ 3^d h^(-d)𝒩 for h≤1. This yields k≤N and preserves the stated N^(-1/d) bounds in both results.
issues.why_classification: The false identification of an arbitrary-translate covering number with a fixed-tiling cell count cannot be repaired by a notation edit. A genuine geometric counting argument and an admissible-scale restriction are required. That work is contained, and the loss of only the finite initial N range leaves a recognizably comparable lattice theorem and the same asymptotic rate, so the issue is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Unshifted pixel grid can exceed N cells

failure_location.quote: Setting $h=N^{-\frac1d}$ yields $N$ cubes of length $N^{-\frac1d}$ in the unit cube

issues.failure_explanation: For d=2 and N=4, the old spacing is 1/2. Along each coordinate, the three cells centered at -1/2, 0, and 1/2 meet the open interval (-1/2,1/2), so nine cells meet the interior square. Placing positive mass in each intersection gives nine nonzero atoms, contradicting the at-most-four claim. Rounding and boundary alignment therefore cannot be ignored.
issues.overall_effect: The at-most-N assertions for the old Dirac and indicator pixel-grid corollaries fail, although their lattice-spacing error estimates remain of order N^{-1/d}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For both pixel corollaries, let M=floor(N^(1/d)) and use the aligned grid M^(-1)(ℤ^d+s), where s=0 when M is odd and s=(1/2,…,1/2) when M is even. Exactly M^d≤N cells then meet the cube interior. The same cellwise couplings give Dirac error at most √d/(2M) ≤ √d N^(-1/d) and indicator error at most √d/M ≤ 2√d N^(-1/d).
issues.why_classification: The unshifted construction genuinely violates the term budget, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the floor-and-parity shift is an elementary local alignment correction requiring no new lemma or proof architecture. It preserves the all-N term cap, the uniform-grid method, and the N^(-1/d) rate, with only immaterial constant changes.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The choice of the scaling factor and shift on the integer lattice ensures that there are at most $N$ Voronoi cells that intersect the unit cube.

issues.title: Point indicators in piecewise-constant corollaries
issues.failure_explanation: The corollary claims a piecewise-constant probability approximation, but 1_{hλ} is the indicator of a singleton and is zero Lebesgue-almost everywhere. Thus the displayed sum has total mass zero rather than one. The invoked THM:LatticePiecewiseConstant proves the claim for 1_{V_{hλ}}, not for the printed point indicators.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed approximants in the three piecewise corollaries are not probability densities, so their Wasserstein distances and claimed approximation bounds are not defined as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In each of the three piecewise-constant corollaries, replace the singleton indicator by the associated cell indicator and use the matching cell volume: ν(V_{hλ})|V_{hλ}|^(-1)1_{V_{hλ}} in the scaled-lattice formulas and ν(V_λ)|V_λ|^(-1)1_{V_λ} in the pixel formula. No proof argument needs to change.
issues.why_classification: The old source itself uniquely forces the cell indicators: the general approximation form, THM:LatticePiecewiseConstant, the volume normalization, and the surrounding prose all specify piecewise-constant densities on Voronoi cells. The proofs invoke that theorem and never reason from singleton indicators. The repeated occurrences are therefore copied transcription errors despite their severe literal effect.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: In the case with $\tau_{i} = \one_{V_{i}}$, we see that $\mu_N = \sum_{i} \frac{\mu(V_{i})}{|V_{i}|} \one_{V_{i}}$.

issues.title: Annular tail normalization for nonintegral R
issues.failure_explanation: Writing R=m+r with 0<r<1 gives a first denominator 1-r<1, so Σ_{j≥⌊R⌋}(j+1-R)^{-2}>Σ_{n≥1}n^{-2}=π²/6. The hypotheses allow an admissible counterexample: for p=d=1, R=0.6 and ε=0.1, item (ii) permits singular-continuous mass 0.3 concentrated near |x|=1, with the remaining mass at 0, while its projection cost is approximately 0.3·0.4=0.12>ε.
issues.overall_effect: The singular-continuous component can exceed its allocated ε^p/3 cost, so THM:noncompact_ext and the later noncompact approximation corollary are false for admissible nonintegral radii.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let m=floor(R) and replace the singular-continuous hypothesis by μ⊥(B_(j,j+1]) ≤ (ε^p/3)(6/π²)/[(j+1-R)^p(j+1-m)^2] for every integer j≥m. Then ∑_{j≥m}(j+1-R)^p μ⊥(B_(j,j+1]) ≤ (ε^p/3)(6/π²)∑_{n≥1}n^(-2)=ε^p/3. Carry this corrected hypothesis into the dependent noncompact approximation corollary.
issues.why_classification: The proof uses a false shifted-series comparison, so mathematical correction is required. The displayed replacement is a local normalization of the same annular decay premise, agrees with the original condition for integral R, retains every radius and the same tail order, and leaves the projection method, ε budget, and downstream approximation rate unchanged.

issues.title: Absolute-continuous tail normalization omits R
issues.failure_explanation: The underbraced radial integral is ∫_R^∞r^{-2}dr=1/R, which is not at most 1 when 0<R<1. This is not merely a loose proof bound: for d=p=1, one may take the absolutely continuous tail proportional to ε|x|^{-3} outside a sufficiently small R and put the remaining probability mass inside B_R. It satisfies the printed envelope, but its projection cost is proportional to ε/R and can exceed ε.
issues.overall_effect: The absolutely continuous component can exceed its ε^p/3 budget for small truncation radii, invalidating THM:noncompact_ext and the noncompact approximation corollary that adds ε to the compact approximation error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize the absolutely continuous tail hypothesis by requiring f_μ(x) ≤ ε^p R(p+1)/(3C|x|^(p+d+1)) for |x|>R. Replace the erroneous estimate by the exact calculation ∫_R^∞(r-R)^p r^(-p-2)dr=1/[R(p+1)], which restores the ε^p/3 budget. Propagate this corrected premise to the dependent noncompact approximation corollary.
issues.why_classification: The proof relies on an incorrect radial integral, so the defect is not transcriptional. Its complete repair is a one-line integral calculation and a local R-dependent normalization of the same power-law tail condition. All radii, the truncation construction, the conclusion, and the dependent approximation rate remain intact.
